goal.decided: The accounting team prints each client's invoice from the line items they keep in their spreadsheet, at that client's tax rate, without writing any Python. Once it holds, a colleague from accounting saves the line items from the spreadsheet, runs one command with the client's tax rate, and gets the invoice with its subtotal, tax, and total, by the README alone.

deliverables.name: An accountant prints an invoice from the line items saved from their spreadsheet with one command, setting the client's tax rate on it

decisions.decided: Each line `<description>;<price>;<quantity>`, as invoicer/lines.py parse_lines reads it
The rate as the decimal that invoicer/tax.py tax_of multiplies the subtotal by, such as 0.19
`invoicer <line-items file> --rate <rate>` prints the invoice as invoicer/render.py render gives it on standard output; pyproject.toml installs it as the console script `invoicer`
One test for each refusal case, named by its case, and two tests that print a two-line invoice at 0.19 and at another rate, showing the rate is set per invoice

Refuses a missing or unreadable file, a line not `<description>;<price>;<quantity>`, a price not a number, a quantity not a whole number, and a missing rate or one outside 0 to 1 (such as 19 for 0.19): prints nothing of the invoice, writes on standard error the line number or value and the form expected, and exits non-zero

deliverables.name: A colleague from accounting prints a client's invoice by the README alone, without writing any Python
